Europe in 1453: look where the Byzantine Empire used to be. The Ottomans took its last city in 53 days, and two of the tricks that decided it are easy to miss on a map.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The siege of Constantinople ran from 6 April to 29 May 1453. The attacker was Mehmed II, who had become sultan at 19 and was about 21 when the city fell.
2/ The defenders numbered roughly 7,000-8,000. Modern estimates put the Ottoman army at 50,000-80,000. Fewer than 50,000 people lived inside the walls, refugees included.
3/ The Ottomans had a giant bombard built by a Hungarian engineer called Orban: about 27 feet long, able to throw a stone ball weighing some 600 pounds over a mile. Reloading took around three hours.
4/ The defenders stretched a chain across the Golden Horn to keep ships out. On 22 April Mehmed answered by having ships dragged overland on greased logs, past the chain and into the harbour.
5/ The Genoese commander Giovanni Giustiniani arrived with about 700 men and led the land-wall defence. When he was badly wounded in the final assault, his withdrawal caused panic on the walls.
6/ Constantinople became the Ottoman capital, replacing Adrianople. Hagia Sophia was turned into a mosque. Emperor Constantine XI's fate is unknown: tradition says he died fighting in the streets.
